correctness.rationale: For strictly positive iid atomless costs the two PF inequalities reduce to 2+(1-t)F'(t)≥2 and 2-tF'(t)≥2 for F=Σ log(b_i+t(a_i-b_i)). F''<0 except simultaneous indifference; thus exactly one or three distinct PF lottery allocations a.s., three iff F'(0)>0>F'(1). Under opposite preferences r=a1/b1,s=b2/a2∈(0,1), independent with conditional CDF H, the derivative signs are exactly max(0,2-1/r)<s<1/(2-r). The two orientations total probability 1/2. Independent SymPy integration reproduces H_uniform(r)=r and H_exp(r)=2r/(1+r), yielding log2−1/2 and log3/4. A separate exact rational test of 1260 nondegenerate integer-cost profiles verified endpoint/interior counts. Atomlessness makes equality boundaries null; the iid ratio law is not assumed universal beyond H.

value.rationale: Multiplicity probability is a natural quantitative economic diagnostic explicitly motivated by the earlier bads-equilibrium random-prevalence question. The contrast 0.193147 (uniform) vs 0.274653 (exponential) under identical ordinal preferences isolates cardinal tail effects; arbitrary atomless-H Stieltjes law is a reusable two-alternative benchmark, not a generic claim for more agents.
